proposition: As MK reports them, Nafsat I says Ibn Turka studied only tafsir, hadith, uṣūl and fiqh for 15 years abroad, while the R. Iʿtiqādiyya says he explored suspect sciences in his youth. The two self-reports sit uneasily together; MK does not draw this contrast on the pages read here. This is the researcher's observation, not MK's.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, writing to the ruler who was judging him
Melvin-Koushki, The Quest for a Universal Science (Yale 2012)
